🖥 War not always the solution, Iran can overcome challenges: Pezeshkian

📌 Tehran, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian has emphasized that “war is not always the solution”, adding that Iran can overcome issues through prudence.

Addressing a conference in Tehran on Wednesday, Pezeshkian praised the resilience of various segments of Iranian society during the recent US-Israeli war of aggression.
​
“But war is not always the solution,” the president said, emphasizing that issues that can be resolved through reason and diplomacy should not be dealt with through confrontation.
​
Pezeshkian added that Iran can navigate its current circumstances through “prudence and thought” and move toward dignity and national pride.
​
The president also hailed the Islamabad memorandum of understanding (MoU) as a source of pride for the Islamic Republic, saying global analyses have recognized Iran as the victor in the confrontation.
​
Referring to Imam Ali’s (PBUH) directive to his governor, Malik al-Ashtar, on peace, Pezeshkian said a peace proposal from an enemy should not be rejected if it serves God’s satisfaction, as peace brings relief to soldiers and security to the people and markets.
​
At the same time, he stressed the importance of remaining vigilant after peace is reached. Pezeshkian noted that Imam Ali (PBUH), while advising the acceptance of peace, repeatedly warned against complacency, as the enemy could approach and launch a surprise attack.
​
He said the warning should not be viewed as opposition to peace, but rather as a call for prudence, sound judgment, caution and foresight.
​
Although Iran does not trust the enemy, Tehran will seek to overcome the crisis through prudent measures, he said.
​
The president noted that some forces do not want Iran to become a powerful country, but stressed that it can move forward through wise policymaking, adherence to the guidance of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei, and coordination among the heads of the three branches of government.
​
Pezeshkian emphasized strength, unity, and domestic solidarity, adding that despite the pressure and the war, Iran has stood firm and will continue on its path.

📲 @Irna_en​

The AI Illusion

One of the most interesting things in the AI industry today, and something that remains outside the attention of 99.9% of people, is the real impact of artificial intelligence on the economy.

Hyperscalers are investing hundreds of billions of dollars in AI infrastructure. Corporations are spending billions on tokens and on attempts to integrate AI into their operations. And the entire market is being accelerated by everyone buying from each other in a loop, valuations rising, more capital flowing in, and the market continuing to expand.

But the question that I think is actually worth asking is this: how much is artificial intelligence really affecting the economy and GDP today?

I think you may be surprised, but if you try to estimate it and look at the actual data rather than the perception created by society and social media, the impact of AI on GDP today is approximately zero percent.

In simple terms, the hundreds of billions of dollars invested so far have not yet produced any noticeable additional economic growth.

Does this mean AI is useless? Of course not.

Over the next several years, there is a very high probability that this number will change and AI will genuinely create enormous additional value.

But the data we see today tells us something different. The speed at which artificial intelligence is being integrated into society, the economy, and the world has been significantly overestimated.

And at some point, these expectations will be corrected, and the entire industry will correct along with them.
